subject: Service pressure: rapid throughput collapse + p99 tail — cross-team triage and customer note
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T09:12:03-07:00
Subject: Observability alert: sudden throughput drop and p99 tail increase — first pass

Team,

Monitoring picked up a sustained throughput collapse on gen-api between 08:58–09:05 PT for a subset of instances serving Cartline traffic. QPS down ~45% and p99 increased from 320ms to 2.4s. No full service outage but customer impact is visible (error rate up ~0.6%, inflated latencies).

Quick notes:
- Affected instances: eu-west-2 and us-west-2 partitions serving Cartline route (gen-v1).
- Recent runtime change: small kernel scheduling tweak deployed 04:00 PT that touched KV cache eviction thresholds (canary).
- Alerting: SLO breaching p99; I've escalated to on-call.

I'm attaching the initial metrics snapshot and the alert window. Starting triage now — tagging Ben and Karthik for runtime/kernel angle.

Soojin
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: perf-heapdump-20290415.tar.gz (metrics + flamegraphs)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T09:22:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability alert: sudden throughput drop and p99 tail increase — first pass

On it — thanks for the heads up. Initial look at the heapdump and CPU traces shows a pattern consistent with KV cache thrashing: frequent evictions followed by repeated KV loads, which spikes per-request CPU and serialization latency. The recent kernel scheduling change could have reduced run-queue priority for the KV maintenance thread.

Actions I'm kicking off now:
1) Revert the kernel scheduling tweak in the canary fleet (target within 20m).
2) Increase KV retention window by +30% (config flag rollbackable).
3) Collect end-to-end traces for 30 minutes post-change and share s3 link.

I've opened JIRA-REDW-2134 and attached a perf snapshot. If the revert looks clean we can push a hotfix and follow up with a short customer note.

-Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sre-bridgereport.pdf
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T10:03:45-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability alert: sudden throughput drop and p99 tail increase — first pass

Thanks Ben / Soojin.

Two product / customer asks while you triage:
- Impact framing: I need a crisp one-paragraph explanation I can send to Cartline leadership (alex.reed@cartline.com). Keep it non-technical: what went wrong, what we are doing now, and when we expect normal service.
- Roadmap ask: if this is KV retention config volatility, can we prioritize a short-term guardrail (config drift detection + automated revert) on the roadmap? If yes, approximate timeline (days/weeks).

Also attaching the customer-visible metrics (extracted from RB) so we can quantify user impact for the note. I can draft the outbound after I have the language.

-steph
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: customer-impact-metrics.csv
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Triage update — suspected KV eviction loop; mitigation plan and ETA

Update from on-call and Eng:
- Root cause hypothesis: KV cache eviction acceleration after the scheduling tweak lowered maintenance thread throughput. That produced repeated cache misses for long-lived prefixes, amplifying per-request work and causing p99 tail.
- Immediate mitigations applied (09:45–10:20 PT): reverted scheduling tweak in canary, increased KV retention window on affected instances, and applied request-level soft-throttling for heavy Cartline routes to prevent cascading CPU pressure.

Preliminary impact: p99 reduced from 2.4s -> ~480ms in canaries; QPS recovering to ~85% of baseline. We'll keep the soft-throttle for 2–4 hours while collecting traces.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Ben: validate revert across all affected partitions and confirm p99 stability (ETA 2h).
- Karthik: prepare rollback plan for the runtime change in case subtle regressions appear (ETA 1.5h).
- Stephanie: please review the customer note draft below and mark / edit.

Soojin
SRE, Redwood Inference

Note: We'll attach a post-change performance snapshot to the customer note once Ben confirms.
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@cartline.com>, ops@cartline.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T12:30:25-07:00
Subject: DRAFT: Brief on degraded performance (Cartline) — do not send yet

DRAFT — do not send.

Alex / Cartline team,

We wanted to reach out about an issue that briefly impacted your API performance this morning. Between ~08:58–09:05 PT we saw elevated latencies and a partial reduction in throughput for requests routed to your gen-v1 route. Our engineers identified the cause as an interaction between a runtime background task and our cache eviction settings that temporarily increased per-request work for some sessions.

What we did immediately:
- Reverted the recent internal runtime change in the canary fleet and increased cache retention for affected instances.
- Applied a temporary rate-smoothing control to avoid cascading CPU pressure while we monitored recovery.

Current state and ETA:
- Performance has improved significantly in canaries; p99 is trending down toward baseline. We expect full normalization within 4 hours, and we'll confirm with a follow-up snapshot.

Next steps:
- We'll share a short postmortem with timeline and root cause analysis within 72 hours.
- If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute sync today to walk through what happened and answer questions.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is disruptive and we're treating it with high priority.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

-----
Please review — prefer non-technical clarity. If Ben / Soojin confirm stabilization earlier I will send an updated note with the snapshot.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@cartline.com>, ops@cartline.com
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-15T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: fix applied and p99 improvement — Cartline impact update

Alex / Cartline ops,

Following up with the actions and early results: we rolled a hotfix (revert + KV retention increase) across all affected partitions at ~12:45 PT. Observed metrics: p99 for Cartline gen-v1 has improved from the peak 2.4s to ~430ms and QPS is at ~98% of baseline. Error rate returned to nominal.

We will:
- Keep monitoring closely for the next 24 hours and share hourly snapshots for the first 4 hours.
- Publish a postmortem within 72 hours with timeline, root cause, and a list of preventive work (config drift detection, stronger runtime gating).
- Offer a 30-minute post-incident review at your convenience — propose 15:30 PT today.

Apologies again for the disruption. If you prefer a written summary only, let us know and we'll deliver that instead.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
